```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
```

This interactive dashboard displays results of the food access examination for thirteen higher educational institutions in Erie County. Click the toggle below for quick access or keep scrolling for a full view of the results.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false title="Quick Access to Results"}

* [Retailer density & distance from institutions](dashboard.qmd#map-density-distance)
* [Number of retailers accepting SNAP/EBT or other voucher programs](dashboard.qmd#dygraph-vouchers)
* [Average store operating hours throughout the week](dashboard.qmd#plot-storehours)
* [Customer feedback & score of available retailers](dashboard.qmd#valuebox-feedback)

:::

### Retailer density and distance from institutions. {#map-density-distance}

```{r}
#| label: institution-map
#| title: "Institution map"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| padding: 0px

library(leaflet)

institutions <- read.csv(
  "data/processed/eriecounty_institutions_geocoded.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)

institutions <- institutions[
  is.finite(institutions$latitude) &
    is.finite(institutions$longitude),
]

if (nrow(institutions) == 0L) {
  stop("No usable coordinates found. Run geocode_institutions.r first.")
}

leaflet(institutions) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    label = ~institution,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<strong>",
      htmltools::htmlEscape(institution),
      "</strong><br>",
      htmltools::htmlEscape(address)
    )
  ) |>
  fitBounds(
    lng1 = min(institutions$longitude) - 0.01,
    lat1 = min(institutions$latitude) - 0.01,
    lng2 = max(institutions$longitude) + 0.01,
    lat2 = max(institutions$latitude) + 0.01
  )
```

***
This *placeholder* map shows the number of retailers around higher education institutions. Additionally, it also displays the distance between an institution and a retailer based on the parameters you set.

### Number of retailers accepting SNAP/EBT or other voucher programs. {#dygraph-vouchers}

```{r}
library(dygraphs)
lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths)
dygraph(lungDeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Diseases in the UK") %>%
  dySeries("mdeaths", label = "Male") %>%
  dySeries("fdeaths", label = "Female") %>%
  dyOptions(stackedGraph = TRUE) %>%
  dyRangeSelector(height = 20) %>% 
  dyRangeSelector()
```

***
This *placeholder* graph shows the affordability of retailers over time by displaying the number of retailers who accept SNAP/EBT or other food voucher programs. Adjust the slider to see in-depth information according to your preference.


### Average store operating hours throughout the week. {#plot-storehours}

```{r}
library(plotly)
p <- ggplot(data = diamonds, aes(x = cut, fill = clarity)) +
            geom_bar(position = "dodge")
ggplotly(p)
```

***
This *placeholder* graph shows you the average operating hours of store throughout the week. Zoom in to see additional details and answer questions like "how many stores are open on a Sunday?" or "how many stores are operational near SUNY Buffalo State v.s. Canisius College?"

### Customer feedback and food access score(s). {#valuebox-feedback}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| include: true
#| output: asis

# Placeholder scores:
# 5 = extremely high food access
# 1 = extremely low food access
scores <- c(5, 4, 3, 4, 5, 2, 4, 3, 5, 4)

average_score <- mean(scores)
review_count <- length(scores)

popup_message <- sprintf(
  paste0(
    "Recommendation score: %.1f / 5\n",
    "Based on %d placeholder reviews.\n\n",
    "5 = extremely high food access\n",
    "1 = extremely low food access"
  ),
  average_score,
  review_count
)

# Safely format the message for an HTML button.
js_message <- as.character(
  jsonlite::toJSON(popup_message, auto_unbox = TRUE)
)

cat(
  '<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" onclick="alert(',
  htmltools::htmlEscape(js_message, attribute = TRUE),
  ')">Show average food access score</button>',
  sep = ""
)
```

***
This *placeholder* scorecard consolidates the food access data examined in this dashboard into an average scoring index, presented from ranges\ 
1 = extremely low food access to\
5 = extremely high food access\

Click the button to view the placeholder result.
